title: NANO BANANA, NEW MODELS GALORE & WHY CHINA MIGHT WIN: Jimmy & Matt debate their favourite AI stories from Nov/Dec 2025
description: Send us Fan Mail Forget the leaderboard for a second—what actually changes your day? We dig into Google’s Gemini 3 and why tight integration across email, search, and docs starts to matter more than raw benchmark wins. Multimodal reasoning with long context finally supports “deep research” workflows that don’t collapse mid-thread, and the new image generation model feels like a leap: crisp multilingual text, many reference images, and grounded outputs that can summarise complex material in a single visual. This isn’t a party trick; it removes whole layers of cleanup that used to swallow hours. We also talk about OpenAI’s quieter 5.1 updates and why Claude Opus 4.5 may be a halo model priced out of everyday use. Then comes the plot twist: DeepSeek 3.2 arrives with sparse attention, delivering comparable performance at about a tenth of the cost. That reframes the game. If efficiency and power availability set the ceiling, not just parameter counts, the centre of gravity tilts toward whoever can build energy and compute cheapest and fastest. We didn't talk about ChatGPT 5.2 because it didn't launch until the day after we recorded! Which leads to the bigger frame: China’s structural advantages in energy buildout, land, and manufacturing, and the West’s constraints around permitting and older grids. If energy is the real bottleneck, policy and infrastructure—not just labs—decide who scales. We map that to the market mood: concentrated gains, circular GPU spending, and thin near-term ROI inside enterprises. It looks frothy, even if the spend sits with giants who can withstand a longer runway. Jobs are already shifting at the edges. Entry roles in analysis and production feel the squeeze, while autonomy scales in the background: robotaxi rides are compounding, and once safety clears a threshold, driving jobs face a systemic reset. The throughline is blunt: the winners pair efficiency with integration and a sane energy story. Benchmarks still matter, but only when they show up as trust, speed, and lower bills. If you enjoy thoughtful, plain‑spoken takes on AI’s real impact, hit follow, share this with a friend, and leave a quick review—what should we dig into next?
summary: The November/December 2025 roundup covers a genuine model bonanza: Gemini 3 retakes the benchmarks with tight integration across Google products, GPT-5.1 lands as a quiet iterative reaction, Claude Opus 4.5 is priced so ludicrously it looks like a benchmark 'halo' model, and DeepSeek 3.2 matches frontier performance at a tenth of the cost via sparse attention. Matt makes the case that China's energy buildout, manufacturing scale and planning advantages may tilt the AI race, while both hosts agree Nano Banana Pro is the year's biggest consumer leap and that the AI-driven stock market concentration is a bubble nearing the shore.
keyTalkingPoints: Gemini 3 topped the benchmarks and beat Claude at coding, but for most users 'best model' matters less than personality, speed and ecosystem integration - and Google's all-in-one subscription now makes it the obvious single choice
GPT-5.1 is an iterative improvement (instant/thinking modes) dropped as a reaction to Gemini 3; Jimmy declares 'they've lost the AI race, I think. Open AI'
Claude Opus 4.5 costs ~10x Sonnet per API token; Jimmy's theory is frontier labs quietly 'turn down' models after release while Opus stays untuned as a halo model nobody actually uses
DeepSeek 3.2 matches frontier models (sometimes beating them) at a tenth of the cost using DeepSeek Sparse Attention - 'another DeepSeek moment' that has been oddly quiet in Western news

Matt argues China is running a 'Manhattan project on energy' with spare grid capacity and cheap manufacturing, while the US cannot build power infrastructure fast enough - 'at best it's neck and neck'

Nano Banana Pro finally renders text flawlessly (including Chinese), takes up to 14 reference images, and can reason through a book's worth of text to produce one grounded visual; jobs data shows 22-25 year olds in AI-exposed roles down 13% and Waymo scaling toward half a million rides a week

jimmy: OpenAI has lost the AI race; GPT-5.1's muted drop was a panicked reaction to Gemini 3
Frontier labs quietly dial models down after release to cut costs, and Opus 4.5 is the untuned halo model kept benchmark-strong
The AI bubble will burst within 6-12 months; it is a classic hype cycle concentrated in big tech and fed by retail investors
The US vs China AI race is 'at best neck and neck' - power infrastructure, not chips or data centers, will decide it
matt: For normal users 'best model' barely matters anymore; Gemini's integration and storage bundle make it the one subscription worth having
DeepSeek is now effectively China's national model and proof that Western chip restrictions have completely backfired
China's long-term planning, land ownership and energy overcapacity give it structural advantages the West's permitting-bound grids cannot match
The AI jobs story is finally producing directly attributable displacement, concentrated among early-career workers
